name: dead-submit-button
description: Customers report that the 'Request a demo' button on the marketing site does nothing — they click it and no confirmation ever appears. Sales is losing leads. Fix it so a customer who enters their email gets a confirmation.
bugs: public/app.js looks up the button by the wrong id (getElementById('submitBtn')) while the button's id is 'submit-btn', so it returns null and the click handler is never attached (the script throws on load)

the validation branch is inverted: it shows the 'invalid email' error when isValidEmail(email) is TRUE, so even after the handler is wired up a valid address is rejected — the confirmation never shows and the field is never cleared
correct_diagnosis: Two bugs: app.js selected the submit button with the wrong id ('submitBtn' vs the actual 'submit-btn') so the click handler never attached, AND the validation check was inverted (it errored when the email WAS valid). Using the correct id wires the handler, and flipping the validation condition so valid input takes the success branch makes the confirmation appear and clears the field; invalid input is still rejected.

reference_fix.description: Use the correct button id AND fix the inverted validation so valid input succeeds.

naive_fix.description: Trap bait: fix only the wrong id (the click now produces a response, so the visible smoke test passes) but leave the inverted validation — valid input is wrongly rejected, so the held-out 'valid email succeeds' regression fails.
